title: Hot and reading clarinet players: George Boyd, Mealy Barnes, Picou
summary: Miller ranks clarinetists, noting who read and who got off, including George Boyd, Mealy Barnes, Picou and Zeb.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Who were the hot clarinet players in the old days?

Well, I don't brag on it, but my boy I had to have me play much clarinet as hot clarinet than anybody I want to hear, George Boyd. He played a whole lot of clarinet. Well, now. Zep was a nice clarinet player, but he didn't play nothing hot. He just, you know. He had to make a hard squeaky note to do.
Mm-hmm. What about, say now you take a guy like Mealy Barnes. Did he ever read any of those, played with any of those reading bands?
I'm going to tell you the truth.

I used to see Mealy Barnes, the band. I believe he played with Chris Kelly. You did. But I never did notice how much playing he used to do. Mm-hmm. I never did. But they tell me Mealy Barnes was a good clarinet player. Yeah, that's what I heard.
But who was the reading clarinet?

William Alfred. Pico, or anything? Pico, yeah. T.O. Mm-hmm. Uh-hmm. Uh, that guy used to play with Robeshow there. Well, Pico, Tico used to play with him. Pico, or Tico, or something they call him. Pico. And, I don't know. Them the ones I know, because Zeb didn't read, Piel didn't read, George didn't read, Handy didn't read.
Well, could those guys get read, the ones who read? How many of them could get really read?
No, that's what I'm telling you now. They couldn't do it. They couldn't do like them other things, but they'd get off right then.
Could T.O. get off? Not much. Pico?
Pico was really saying on high society and them numbers like that, but not get off. He could play them better than anybody. But not get off, I don't know. I don't think he... Not now.

He plays any real variations, you know, now. No. It's the same thing night after night, you know. But he doesn't make up anything as he goes along. Oh no, he don't make up anything, no. Somebody like Melee Bonds, you get the feeling he plays it different every time. Raymond Burke, you know.
Well, like I'm saying about George, boy, he always plays something different.
T.O., yeah, he was a good man, but I never wiped with him. No, Pils.
